Order 
This case is listed today for admission.

2. This Criminal Revision is filed being aggrieved by the order dated 16.6.2023 passed in S.T No.
175/2023 whereby the learned trial Court has framed charges against the applicant under Sections 420, 467, 471 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code.

3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that one Babadeen Baiga had expired on 20.11.2016 but there were three death certificates dated 16.12.2016, 20.11.2016 and 20.1.2017 were issued by Panchayat Secretary Pyarelal Singh and Rojgar Sahayak Jitendra Upadhyay.

Applicant/Revisionist was Bank Manager of Central Bank of India and it is alleged that in connivance with the wife of the deceased Shanti Baiga they have withdrawn Rs.2,00,000/- on 18.7.2017 under the Pradhan Mantri Jandhan Insurance Scheme.

4. Police has filed the charge-sheet on the ground that the applicant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:63064 2 CRR-4194-2023 was enrolled and Trial is going on and there is no stay.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant Revisionist submits that this is a case of zero evidence.
Even if the facts of entire charge-sheet are taken as true then no offence is made out against the applicant.

7. Perused the order and considered the arguments.
8.

The Law regarding discharge is well settled by Hon'ble Supreme Court recently in the judgment dated 18 May 2023 in Cr.A No. 1399/2023 -Captain Manjeet Singh Virdhi (Retired) v. Hussain Mohammed Shattaf and others [2023 LiveLaw (SC) 462] wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in paragraphs 11 and paragraph 12 thus:
'11.

entities.text: Manjeet Singh Virdhi (Retired) v. Hussain Mohammed Shattaf and others [2023 LiveLaw (SC) 462]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The law on issue as to what is to be considered at the time of discharge of an accused is well settled.
It is a case in which the Trial Court had not yet framed the charges.
Immediately after filing of chargesheet, application for discharge was filed.
The settled proposition of law is that at the stage of hearing on the charges entire evidence produced by the prosecution is to be believed.
In case no offence is made out then only an accused can be discharged.
Truthfulness, sufficiency and acceptability of the material produced can be done only at the stage of trial.
At the stage of charge, the Court has to satisfy that a prima facie case is made out against the accused persons.

Interference of the Court at that stage is required only if there is strong reasons to hold that in case the trial is allowed to proceed, the same would amount to abuse of process of the Court.
12.
The law on the point has been summarised in a recent judgment of this Court in State of Rajasthan v. Ashok Kumar Kashyap2.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan v. Ashok Kumar Kashyap2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relevant paras are extracted below: -

In P. Vijayan v. State of Kerala, (2010) 2 SCC 398, this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63064 3 CRR-4194-2023 Court had an occasion to consider Section 227 CrPC What is required to be considered at the time of framing of the charge and/or considering the discharge application has been considered elaborately in the said decision.

entities.text: P. Vijayan v. State of Kerala, (2010) 2 SCC 398
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed and held that at the stage of Section 227, the Judge has merely to sift the evidence in order to find out whether or not there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

It is observed that in other words, the sufficiency of grounds would take within its fold the nature of the evidence recorded by the police or the documents produced before the court which ex facie disclose that there are suspicious circumstances against the accused so as to frame a charge against him.

It is further observed that if the Judge comes to a conclusion that there is sufficient ground to proceed, he will frame a charge under Section 228 CrPC, if not,
he will discharge the accused.

It is further observed that while exercising its judicial mind to the facts of the case in order to determine whether a case for trial has been made out by the prosecution, it is not necessary for the court to enter into the pros and cons of the matter or into a weighing and balancing of evidence and probabilities which is really the function of the court, after the trial starts.

"25.

sentences.text: The parameters which govern the exercise of this jurisdiction have found expression in several decisions of this Court.

It is a settled principle of law that at the stage of considering an application for discharge the court must proceed on the assumption that the material which has been brought on the record by the prosecution is true and evaluate the material in order to determine whether the facts emerging from the material, taken on its face value, disclose the existence of the ingredients necessary to constitute the offence.

In State of T.N. v. N. Suresh Rajan, (2014) 11 SCC 709, adverting to the earlier decisions on the subject, this Court held:
'29. ...

entities.text: State of T.N. v. N. Suresh Rajan, (2014) 11 SCC 709
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this stage, probative value of the materials has to be gone into and the court is not expected to go deep into the matter and hold that the materials would not warrant a conviction.

In our opinion, what needs to be considered is whether there is a ground for presuming that the offence has been committed and not NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63064 4 CRR-4194-2023 whether a ground for convicting the accused has been made out.

To put it differently, if the court thinks that the accused might have committed the offence on the basis of the materials on record on its probative value, it can frame the charge; though for conviction, the court has to come to the conclusion that the accused has committed the offence.
The law does not permit a mini trial at this stage."

9. In this criminal case, Central Bank of India Manager as it is alleged in connivance with the wife of the deceased Shanti Baiga have illegally withdrawn Rs.2,00,000/- on 18.7.2017 under the Pradhan Mantri Jandhan Insurance Scheme and thus committed various offences.

10. In any criminal offence it can be committed by two ways by directly participating and committing an act and secondly remaining neglect and in criminal jurisprudence, act and omission both are punishable but whether one was careless or not is a matter of fact.

It is not a legal proposition that Bank Officer in which fraud is committed in Bank had mes rea or not or he was only careless as he did not verify the documents carefully and what was his mandate regarding the same is again question of fact and has to be proved or disproved in trial Court and facts require recording of evidence in trial Court and recording of evidence is pending.
11. Therefore, in the considered view of this Court all matters have to be sorted out in the trial and there is no ground at this stage to interfere with the framing of charges.
12. Accordingly, this Revision is dismissed at admission stage with liberty to the Revisionist to raise all factual and legal ground before the trial Court at appropriate stage during the trial.
